content.text:
I've submitted index 111 (Bi 0.08, Cu 0.50, V 0.42) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, 1.83 µA. That was the whole merit budget. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so no phases are confirmed.

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Region targeted | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|---|
| **111** | 0.08 / 0.50 / 0.42 | Near 1:1 Cu:V, a copper vanadate (Cu₂V₂O₇) | **1.83 µA** |
| 3 | 0.36 / 0.21 / 0.43 | Near BiVO₄, with about 20% Cu | 0.90 µA |
| 57 | 0.08 / 0.61 / 0.32 | More Cu-rich copper vanadate (Cu₃V₂O₈) | 0.71 µA |

- **How I picked:** the first two measurements tested the two best-known photoanode materials in this system, BiVO₄ and the copper vanadates. The copper-vanadate side came out ahead, so I used the last measurement on a more Cu-rich point. It was worse, which points to the 1:1 Cu:V region as the better one.
- **Why not the model's suggestion:** after two data points, the model's uncertainty was larger than its predictions for every candidate it ranked. Its suggestion wasn't more informative than choosing by known chemistry.
- **Main caveat:** three points cover a 188-composition library very thinly. Nothing close to index 111, such as index 27 or 56, was measured, so a better composition may exist nearby that this campaign didn't reach.
